There appears to be, amongst the readers of this sub and in general everywhere, a fundamental misunderstanding about the Marxist concept of the abolition of private property.

The idea of "taking all your stuff and redistributing it" is wrong.

In Marxian economics and socialist politics, there is distinction between "private property" and "personal property". The former is defined as the means of production in reference to private ownership over an economic enterprise based on socialized production and wage labor; the latter is defined as consumer goods or goods produced by an individual. Prior to the 18th century, private property usually referred to land ownership. When Marx called for the abolition of private property, he was not referring to privately owned personal property such as clothing and furniture that was not used to produce the "social wealth," but to productive property.

(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Private_property#Socialist_perspectives)) (source for above, with citations)

It is the productive wealth that communism aimed to liberate from the consolidated control of the few.

But not the means of production in it's entirety. The following is straight from the communist manifesto:

Hard-won, self-acquired, self-earned property! Do you mean the property of petty artisan and of the small peasant, a form of property that preceded the bourgeois form? There is no need to abolish that; the development of industry has to a great extent already destroyed it, and is still destroying it daily.

What we would equate today with small business is what Marx is referring to above. Communism was never intended to stifle economic growth by removing the incentive to excel, and not intended to punish the successful. It meant to remove the leverage that allowed the most wealthy (many of whom inherited that private property, not created it) to take advantage of the workers required to make those particular engines of production work.

I'm not trying to defend there merit of this (full disclosure, <3 socialism) here, but rather trying to explain what is apparently an often misunderstood aspect of this man's theory.

Full text of the Manifesto of the Communist Party
On the abolition of private property.

Marx's economic analysis was shit in his own day, but it's become much shitter in the meantime. The economy no longer consists mostly of giant factories the way it used to. As a consequence you certainly can't distinguish between personal goods and productive goods.

The laptop in front of me right now I could potentially use to write software worth billions. (I probably won't.)

There are many other reasons that Marx is rubbish, of course, but trying to apply a theory of the way the economy worked in the 1850s to the present day is just stupid.

It is interesting to think Marx was correct about the means of production eventually reaching the point where it is in the hands of the proletariat. With technology the means of production has been opened to millions more people. Technology has becomemore efficient and it is starting to become affordable. Allowing more people to have an ability to generate an income without the factory owners. 50 years from now the means of production and the economy may be much like Marx predicted.
